description_en: This three-bayedphalcāwasdonated in 1665 and isowned by the Maharjans of the Karuṇāmaya Guṭhī. On the day of Nugaḥyaḥ,samayabajiis distributed here. Cvalcā Phalcā was dismantled in 1995 and reconstructed with funds from GTZ/udle. The new structure included a new inscription and incorporated its 19th-century columns and capitals. It was demolished and reconstructed once again in 2019 due to substantial damage from the 2015 earthquakes.
description_ne: तीनवटा कवल भएको यो फल्चा करुणामयगुठीको रूपमा महर्जनहरूको स्वामित्वमा रहेको छ । नुगःयःको दिनमा यस फल्चामा समय वितरण गर्ने गरिन्छ । पुरानो भएकोले यो च्वल्च ४ फल्चालाई सन् १९९५ मा भत्काएर जिटिजेड्को आर्थिक सहयोगमा १९औँ शताब्दीका काष्ठस्तम्भ र नयाँ शिला अभिलेख समेत राखी पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।

references: Sources and references Inscription identification number LAL4007_I_001 Sources Inscription from NS 785, transcription and translation by Dr. Nutan Sharma, 2021) Details transcription from Newari (Pracalit Newari script) Oṃ śreyostu || samvat 785 | sa caitra vaddhi 12 piṃthache || jake bhā- va thaṃkāḍi yāṅa || abharāja bhāvo hākudeva bhāvo, luterāma bhāvo, lugusiṃ- ha bhāvo, jasarāma bhāvo, jayarāma bhāvo, jugarāma bhāvo, jateyā bhū- samohana, śvaku toratā, mādhava- rāma bhāvo chem hoya yāṅā, sa e- vo pithache lāche sa eva so caka śrīmat śrīśrī buṃga bhaṭṭārakāsake pūrṇamī sevā dayaka thva phale svaṃka- vala dayaka juro, thva pale sunāna ju- lasana senakarasā pañcamāhāpā- taka lāka, bhinakarasā utotra Juro ||  śubha || Translation: Oṃ. may all be well. In the dark half of the month of Caitra, in NS 785 (1665 CE), Jake Bhāvo was declared as senior-most member on the 12th day. The group of Abharāja Bhāvo, Hākudeva Bhāvo, Luterāma Bhāvo, Lugusiṃha Bhāvo, Jasarāma Bhāvo, Jayarāma Bhāvo, and Jugarāma Bhāvo made Pūrṇimā (full moon day) Sevā (serving) Group for Buṃgadyaḥ and built the phalcā in the same Pīthache (area) after leaving the same 3 bays ( kavaḥ for the phalcā) while the house of Mādhava Rāma Bhāvo was expanded. It is built facing east in Pithach ẽ L ā chi area. The norm (rule) of worshipping Buṅgadyah ̣ on the day of every full moon is established (Purn ̣ imā sevā). If anyone tries to destroy the phalcā , he/she will have to bear Pa ñ ca Mah ā P ā pa (five worst sins) where as a good-doer of it will be rewarded with happiness and prosperity. May all be well.

historical_events.event_description: This inscription from NS 785 is attached to the eastern wall of the Phalcā. According to the inscription, the Phalcā was constructed with three bays by a group of Bhāvos. This inscription indicates that there used to be two bays previously, thus allowing for the addition of a third one. Above of the inscription one can see a statue of Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara standing intribaṅga āsanawith two hands. The statue is holding a flower of lotus in its left hand and holding its right hand in a gesture ofvarad.Candraandsūryahave also been inscribed on Lokeśvara's left and right sides respectively.This is a fine example of inscription worship. On the top of the inscription, there is an icon of Bungadyaḥ. Worshipping of the inscription equals worshipping the deity. Some say that itt is not allowed there to sit in thephalcāin front of the inscription showing the back of the body. It is considered as an insult like to a king.
The Phalcāwas renovated by GTZ/Udle and Lalitpur Metropolitan City.

The Phalcā was completely dismantled and reconstructed in a 'traditional style' again. New carved pillars were used and the platform was raised in height. The inscription is still there, but the candle stand has been lost.
